e.text: A3 leads at 17.3% vs benchmark 5.0%; asking the Critic how to push further.

e.note: Reading results for A3, A2, A1

critique.summary: All three plans beat the benchmark by more than 3x (15.8–17.3% reach vs 5.0%), driven by the full-campaign Vice drop (188–192 adopters for $2000 in every plan) and day-0 Las Culturistas (70 for $3500). Targeted social ads, the late street team and the $2500 Good Room pop-up return few adopters for their cost, and Bed-Stuy (zone 2) and Long Island City (zone 3) are barely seeded.

findings.finding: A3 has the highest mean reach (17.3%) and the highest 10th percentile (15.4%) at $10.31 per adopter, but its zone social ads (6–7 adopters per $600) and day-32 LES street team (7 for $450) are its weakest buys.

A2 has the broadest spread across districts (Latin pop 13.8%, Podcasts 10.7%) with a tight 15.0–17.8% band, and the Getting Curious ad credited 70 adopters, as many as Las Culturistas, for the same $3500.

A1 dominates Indie rock and Drag Race (24.8%) but has the lowest mean (15.8%) and the weakest 10th percentile (14.1%), and the day-31 Good Room pop-up got only 14 adopters for $2500, the same as a single $300 partner.
The benchmark's broad social ads got 58 adopters for $4680 and its street teams 3–7 each, so taste-targeted media and partners deliver roughly 3.5x lower cost per adopter.

changes.change: In A3, drop social:0, social:1 and street:0 ($1650) and add the Getting Curious podcast (ED9D4C2F) on day 3, trimming partners as needed to fit the budget.
changes.why: Getting Curious credited 70 adopters versus a combined 20 for those three actions, and it lifts reach in the districts A3 underserves.

changes.change: Never use the $2500 Good Room pop-up (popup:68F326C8) on day 31; spend that money on day-0 partners in Bed-Stuy (zone 2) and Long Island City (zone 3).
changes.why: The pop-up got 14 adopters, the same as one $300 partner, and it ran too late for word of mouth, while zones 2 and 3 hold 10.1% of the natural audience with fit of 0.82–0.91.

changes.change: Keep the Vice collab running days 0–34 and Las Culturistas on day 0 in every plan.
changes.why: Together they account for about 260 adopters for $5500 in every plan, and starting early drives the 50–53% word-of-mouth share.

changes.change: In A1, cut the weakest Williamsburg partners (L'Antagoniste, The Narrows, Abe's Pagoda Bar) and reallocate to Lower East Side partners such as New Museum and Bowery Ballroom.
changes.why: Zone 0 holds 6.8% of the audience, and A1's K-pop, country and Uniqlo reach (11.3%) trails A3's (18.3%).

e.note: All three plans beat the benchmark by more than 3x (15.8–17.3% reach vs 5.0%), driven by the full-campaign Vice drop (188–192 adopters for $2000 in every plan) and day-0 Las Culturistas (70 for $3500). Targeted social ads, the late street team and the $2500 Good Room pop-up return few adopters for their cost, and Bed-Stuy (zone 2) and Long Island City (zone 3) are barely seeded.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B2

plan.headline: A24 Coming-of-Age Preview Week at Nitehawk: Vice drop, Las Culturistas, 15 partners in four zones. Projected reach 19.6% of the natural audience (~1,080 adopters) on $10,000.
plan.summary: We are betting on ground seeding: a Vice co-branded drop and a Las Culturistas host-read go out 34 days before launch, alongside 15 partners across Williamsburg, the Lower East Side, Bed-Stuy and Long Island City. Qloo taste data shows this audience over-indexes on Vice (0.96) and Las Culturistas (0.90), and every partner sits at 0.90–0.94 affinity, mostly through Lady Bird and A24 fans. In the simulation this reaches 19.6% (range 17.4%–21.5%) at $9.26 per adopter, with 54% coming from word of mouth, versus 5.0% for a broad-ads benchmark; these are simulation projections built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee.

weeks.label: Day 34 (kickoff)
items: Launch the Vice co-branded drop ($2,000) and keep it running through launch.
Air the Las Culturistas host-read with Matt Rogers and Bowen Yang ($3,500).
Go live at all 15 partners at once ($300 each): flyers, posters and cards at each location.

weeks.label: Weeks 1–2 (days 34–21)
items: Check that materials are visible at every partner, including New Museum and Bowery Ballroom exits, the Good Room bar and the Stonefruit counter.
Restock cards at high-traffic spots: Music Hall of Williamsburg, Isola Brooklyn and Dun-Well Doughnuts.

weeks.label: Weeks 3–4 (days 20–7)
items: Give the weakest placements (Nostrand Coffee Roaster, Bowery Ballroom, Water's Edge) a refresh and better placement.
Keep the Vice drop visible and point people to Nitehawk tickets.

weeks.label: Launch week (days 6–0)
items: Final restock at all partners, with screening dates and times shown clearly.
Run preview screenings at Nitehawk Williamsburg.
